title: Optimize Guardrails — Success Metrics & KPIs (Targets + Definitions)
content:
SHEET: Optimize Guardrails — Success Metrics & KPIs
Last reviewed: 2025-02-12 (Aditya / Jonas / Logan)

Purpose
- Align Product/Applied ML/Platform/SRE on what “success” means for Optimize Guardrails gating.
- Provide measurable targets by quarter for: regressions prevented, cost savings preserved, gating health, and operational overhead.
- Define data sources and implementation notes so KPIs are computable (not slideware).

Rollout phases (for context)
- Phase A: Observe-only (no blocking) — collect gating outcomes + compare to post-change quality signals
- Phase B: Soft-block (override allowed behind feature flag + RBAC)
- Phase C: Hard-block (default for eligible changes; override requires justification + audit)

Assumptions / notes (read before using targets)
- “Optimize apply” refers to applying a proposed config delta (batching/caching/quantization/routing tweaks) through Console or API.
- Eligible applies are those that would materially change inference behavior/cost (see policy in PM-844).
- Many quality issues are not perfectly attributable; we use a conservative attribution model for “prevented regressions” (see definition).

TAB 1 — KPI SUMMARY (Executive)

Table: Primary KPIs (what we report in launch/exec updates)
| KPI ID | KPI name | Why it matters | Primary owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Quality regressions prevented (est.) | Main user promise: cost optimizations without silent quality drops | Selene Huang / Jonas Weber |
| P2 | Cost savings preserved (net) | Ensure guardrails doesn’t nullify Optimize value | Nadia Rahman |
| P3 | Gating coverage of eligible applies | Guardrails only works if broadly enforced | Ethan Park / Aditya Rao |
| P4 | False positive rate (block-but-should-pass) | Avoid friction + support burden | Sana Farid |
| P5 | Override rate + override outcomes | Keep “escape hatch” rare and auditable | Sean Gallagher / Naomi Feldman |
| P6 | Gating reliability (job latency/error budget) | If runner is flaky, product becomes unusable | Sean Gallagher |

TAB 2 — KPI DEFINITIONS + TARGETS (Quarterly)

Definitions: key terms
- “Apply attempt”: user action attempting to apply an Optimize proposal (Console button or API call).
- “Gating run”: eval-harness run in gating mode producing pass/fail/timeout + metric deltas.
- “Blocked”: apply not executed because gating failed / timed out / runner unavailable, per enforcement mode.
- “Post-change quality incident”: support escalation or internal signal that indicates quality regression after an apply.

Targets are by calendar quarter (Q2 2025 is first pilot quarter in this sheet).

Table: KPI targets by quarter
| KPI ID | KPI name | Definition (metric) | Target Q2'25 (Pilot) | Target Q3'25 (Expanded) | Target Q4'25 (GA) | Target Q1'26 | Data source(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Quality regressions prevented (est.) | Count of applies that would have caused a “material regression” but were blocked by gating. Estimation method: (blocked_due_to_quality_fail) * PPV, where PPV is calibrated via retrospective analysis of historical applies + sentinel prompt sets. | 5–15 / quarter | 20–40 / quarter | 40–80 / quarter | 60–120 / quarter | OptimizeConfigChange audit events + gating results + support/Jira + post-change quality signals | Conservative reporting: publish range until PPV stabilizes. PPV updated monthly during pilot. |
| P2 | Cost savings preserved (net) | Net realized $ savings from Optimize applies that pass gating, compared to baseline config. Formula (monthly): sum(cost_baseline - cost_after) across gated applies; subtract additional eval infra cost (runner GPU hours) and any rollback overhead. | >= $50k | >= $200k | >= $500k | >= $700k | Cost attribution pipeline (token costs), Optimize proposal records, eval runner infra costs | “Preserved” emphasizes we’re not blocking too much. Track per optimization type. |
| P3 | Gating coverage of eligible applies | % of eligible apply attempts that have a completed gating decision (pass/fail) before apply is executed. (eligible_with_decision / eligible_attempts) | >= 70% | >= 85% | >= 95% | >= 97% | Optimize apply logs + gating job store | Coverage is sensitive to timeouts + runner availability. |
| P4 | False positive rate | % of blocked applies where subsequent rerun (same inputs) passes OR manual review (Applied ML) concludes “should have passed.” (false_blocks / total_blocks) | <= 12% | <= 8% | <= 5% | <= 4% | Triage tags in guardrails failures playbook + rerun tool + Applied ML review labels | Requires consistent labeling in triage workflow. Pilot includes weekly adjudication. |
| P5 | False negative rate (proxy) | % of passed applies that are followed by a post-change quality incident within 7 days, for routes covered by prompt sets. (incidents_after_pass / passes) | <= 2.0% | <= 1.5% | <= 1.0% | <= 0.8% | Support tickets + anomaly detection + route health metrics + gating pass logs | Proxy only; many incidents are unrelated. Use “covered routes” filter. |
| P6 | Override rate | Overrides / eligible applies under soft-block or hard-block modes. | <= 6% | <= 4% | <= 2% | <= 2% | Audit events (override=true) + RBAC logs | If override > target, indicates threshold too strict or comms/UX unclear. |
| P7 | Override outcome quality | % of overrides that later trigger a post-change quality incident within 7 days. | <= 5% | <= 4% | <= 3% | <= 3% | Audit events + support/anomaly signals | Overrides should be “rare + informed.” If high, tighten RBAC / require second approver. |
| P8 | Gating decision latency (p95) | p95 time from apply attempt to gating decision available in UI/API. | <= 12 min | <= 8 min | <= 5 min | <= 5 min | Eval runner job metrics + console timing events | Latency includes queue time; isolate dedicated gating worker pool. |
| P9 | Gating timeout rate | % of gating runs that end in timeout. | <= 6% | <= 3% | <= 1% | <= 1% | Eval runner metrics | Timeouts should drop after caching and suite-slimming. |
| P10 | Runner availability (SLO) | % of time gating runner is healthy enough to accept jobs (control-plane perspective). | >= 99.0% | >= 99.5% | >= 99.9% | >= 99.9% | SRE service checks + job queue health | If unavailable, apply behavior depends on tier (blocked vs manual approval). |
| P11 | Audit completeness | % of OptimizeConfigChange audit events that include required guardrails fields (suite_id, suite_rev, prompt_set_rev, threshold_policy_version, decision, reason_codes). | >= 95% | >= 98% | >= 99.5% | >= 99.5% | Audit pipeline validation | Security/compliance asks for this (see audit event spec). |
| P12 | Support burden delta | # of support tickets per 1000 applies tagged “Optimize/Guardrails” + median time-to-resolution (TTR). | <= 3.0 / 1k; TTR <= 3d | <= 2.5 / 1k; TTR <= 3d | <= 2.0 / 1k; TTR <= 2d | <= 2.0 / 1k; TTR <= 2d | Jira SUP tags + Support analytics | Expect initial spike in pilot due to education; should trend down with UX/docs. |

TAB 3 — OPERATIONAL / HEALTH METRICS (SRE)

Table: Alertable indicators (not necessarily “success” KPIs)
| Metric | Definition | Suggested alert threshold | Owner | Dashboard panel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gating_job_backlog | # queued gating jobs waiting > 2 min | warn > 200; page > 500 for 10m | Rafael Mendes | Guardrails / Runner Health |
| gating_worker_error_rate | worker errors / job attempts | warn > 2% for 15m; page > 5% for 10m | Sean Gallagher | Guardrails / Runner Health |
| gating_decision_missing | applies executed without gating decision (should be ~0 post-GA) | warn > 0.2%; page > 1% | Ethan Park | Guardrails / Coverage |
| cache_hit_rate | eval result cache hits / total eval requests | warn < 40% (pilot); target > 65% (GA) | Logan Wright | Guardrails / Efficiency |

TAB 4 — DATA SOURCES & IMPLEMENTATION NOTES

Event sources
1) Audit log: OptimizeConfigChange (authoritative)
- Required fields (subset):
  - tenant_id (hashed), project_id (optional), route_id (optional), environment (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - model_id, model_version
  - optimization_type (quantization|batching|caching|routing)
  - config_delta_id
  - gating: decision (pass|fail|timeout|runner_unavailable), reason_codes, threshold_policy_version
  - eval: suite_id, suite_revision, prompt_set_id, prompt_set_revision, sample_size
  - override: override_used (bool), override_justification (string, redacted rules), override_actor_role
  - timestamps: requested_at, decision_at, applied_at

2) Eval runner metrics
- Job timings, retries, timeouts, worker errors, queue depth.

3) Quality signals after apply (proxies)
- Support tickets (Jira) tagged Optimize + quality regression
- Customer-reported incidents in Slack Connect (when applicable) — not always structured
- Automated anomaly detection (route-level) on:
  - increased user retry rate / abandonment
  - increased “invalid JSON / schema parse failure” for structured output routes
  - spike in tool-calling errors (missing required tool fields)
  - spike in toxicity/factuality heuristic flags (low confidence)

4) Cost metrics
- Token-level cost attribution (per tenant/route/model) maintained by Nadia’s pipeline.
- Compute eval infra cost as (runner_gpu_hours * internal_rate) + storage for artifacts.

Attribution model notes (P1 and P5)
- We do NOT claim causal prevention unless:
  A) gating failed on a metric tied to known regression mode for that optimization type, AND
  B) retrospective evaluation (rerun on “candidate” config) shows regression beyond threshold, AND
  C) prompt-set coverage is tagged as “representative” for the route/workload.
- During pilot, report P1 as a range using PPV calibration (weekly).

TAB 5 — BREAKDOWNS (for analysis)

Recommended breakdown dimensions (use sparingly to avoid cardinality blowups)
- optimization_type
- model_family (e.g., llama, qwen, mistral; internal canonical mapping)
- deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
- tenant_tier (free|pro|enterprise)
- workload_tag (chat|tool_calling|structured_output|embeddings) [note: embeddings generally out-of-scope for “quality” gating]
- suite_id (small, bounded set)

Metrics that should NOT be high-cardinality
- prompt text (never)
- raw customer identifiers (never)
- route names as freeform strings (use normalized route_id)

TAB 6 — OPEN QUESTIONS / TODO
- Decide official definition for “material regression” for exec reporting: single metric breach vs composite “stoplight.” (Selene + Sana)
- Finalize PPV calibration approach and how it changes over time as thresholds improve. (Jonas)
- Confirm internal $/GPU-hour rate to use for eval infra cost in P2 (Finance + Nadia)
- Align with SRE on what counts as runner “availability” vs “degraded” (partial outages) for P10. (Sean)
- Support tagging: standardize Jira fields/labels for guardrails outcomes to compute P12 reliably. (Owen)

Change log (manual)
- 2025-01-17: Created initial KPI list from kickoff notes.
- 2025-02-03: Added cost-preserved net definition and separated false positive/negative proxies.
- 2025-02-12: Updated latency/timeout targets based on runner prototype benchmarks + caching PR plan.
